ai.description: This 40mm frog has a globular body with a dark brown back featuring irregular yellow or white marbling. It is distinguished by a narrow head, a small mouth, and smooth, glandular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uperodon montanus* is best distinguished by the distinct, bright white or yellowish spots scattered across its dark, brownish-black dorsal skin.
ai.habitat: *Uperodon montanus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Jerdon's Ramanella is primarily nocturnal and terrestrial, often emerging from tree hollows or crevices to forage for ants and termites during the monsoon season.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon montanus* breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of eggs in water-filled tree holes or rock crevices.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uperodon montanus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring in moist forests and plantations at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Uperodon montanus* is a series of short, high-pitched metallic "peep" notes, typically heard from tree holes in moist evergreen forests.
